turns.question: Can I buy the battery packs from Brightcell Energy? They quote £104.
turns.reply:
No, you cannot buy battery packs from Brightcell Energy today.

Brightcell Energy is not yet active in the supplier master, so orders cannot be placed with them until they complete onboarding under SOP-PUR-001 (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.1, § 6.3). Battery packs are lithium-cell parts, meaning an order may only be placed once a valid UN 38.3 test report is on file in Ledgerline (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.2). Brightcell's test report is currently undergoing renewal and is not expected until December 2026 (2026-10-22_Quotation Q-BE-26-0917 - Brightcell Energy.eml, § body). Furthermore, a cheaper quotation alone does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part when an existing rate contract is in place (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.4).

passages.text:
Dear Ms Clarke,

Thank you for your call. As promised, our quotation Q-BE-26-0917 for battery packs, 36 V 500 Wh, compatible with your BAT-500 mounting: £104.00 per pack, delivered (DAP) to Manchester, minimum order 500 packs, lead time six weeks from order.

Brightcell Energy is based in Lyon (12 rue des Tanneurs, 69007 Lyon, France). We would be pleased to be set up as a new supplier; our sales administration can send our company documents.

Our UN 38.3 test report is being renewed with our laboratory and the new report is expected in December 2026.

Kind regards,

Julien Marchand

Key account manager, Brightcell Energy

passages.cite: BHT-01 v3, pp.1-6, § BHT-01 Battery handling
passages.text:
BHT-01 Battery handling
Course BHT-01, version 3, November 2025
Quality department
Why battery safety matters
• Lithium cells store a lot of energy
• Damage can show days later
• Most incidents start with a dropped pack
Storage
• Fire cells BAT-Z1 to BAT-Z4 in Manchester main stores
• No more than 1,500 packs per cell
• State of charge 30% to 50%
Damaged packs
• Red quarantine bin in BAT-Z4
• NCR on QA-NCR-02 in the same shift
• Never put a dropped pack back on the shelf
Shipping
• UN3480 for a pack alone
• UN3481 for a pack in or with a bike
• Carrier service DGX
Refresher
• Repeat BHT-01 every 24 months

Action: Remind the stores supervisors that all transfer tickets must be entered into the system before the close of each shift.
Price increases proposed by the primary rim supplier were discussed. A formal notification was received via letter requesting an uplift on all cold-drawn aluminium sections, citing rising energy tariffs at their rolling mill. It was agreed that purchasing cannot accept the revised terms without prior consultation, as existing forward orders were placed under the annual agreement. The buyer pointed out that alternative sources for suitable extrusions are limited without requiring fresh testing on the wheel-truing rigs.
Action: Draft a formal response to the rim supplier holding deliveries to the terms of the existing annual agreement.
The meeting turned to carrier performance for inward freight arriving from the south. The road haulier currently contracted for palletised freight has missed several morning booking slots at Manchester, resulting in wagons being turned away when the bays were fully occupied. This has pushed receipt entries into the following day and distorted lead-time records on the purchasing screens.

6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in
the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in
Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired
certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed
with them.
6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not
by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

6. Supplier qualification
6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors and any other item marked lithium-cell in the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired certificate counts as no certificate.
6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed with them.
7. Prices
7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for reference only.
7.2 Any order at a rate more than 5% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the remarks.

passages.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.3, § What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors
passages.text:
What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?
Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them
with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If
the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order
may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer
a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply
because they provide a cheaper quotation.
Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?
No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier
master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process

passages.cite: POL-BAT-004 v1.2, p.1, § 1. Purpose and scope
passages.text:
1. Purpose and scope
1.1 This policy covers every lithium-cell part at Northbridge: battery packs, cells, hub and mid-drive
motors, chargers and any item with the lithium-cell flag in the item master. Buying these parts is
covered by Purchase Policy POL-PUR-001 §6.2 and Supplier Policy POL-SUP-003 §4.
1. Purpose and scope

passages.cite: SOP-PUR-001 v3.1, p.5, § 6. Timing and system checks
passages.text:
6. Timing and system checks
6.1 Allow five working days from a complete file (POL-SUP-003 §3.6). For a supplier of lithium-cell
parts, allow at least ten working days: the certificate check often needs questions back to the supplier's
test laboratory.
6.2 Ledgerline will not stop you. A new supplier is ACTIVE the moment it is created, and Ledgerline
does not check certificates when an order is saved (parameter PUR.CERT_CHK is N at Northbridge).
The checklist in step 5.8 is the only control.
6. Timing and system checks

5. Procedure
5.1 A new requirement above £100,000 gross needs three written quotations, compared on form
NBC-F-118.
5.2 Items with a current rate contract need no quotation: order at the contract rate (POL-PUR-001
§7.1).
5.3 A quotation from a supplier that is not in the supplier master starts the onboarding procedure
(SOP-PUR-001). It may not be accepted until the supplier is onboarded.
5.4 For lithium-cell parts, compare quotations only from suppliers with a valid UN 38.3 certificate.
Price alone never decides.
5. Procedure: notes and common mistakes

passages.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, pp.2-3, § Appendix A. Definitions
passages.text:
Appendix A. Definitions
Term | Meaning
Gross value | Basic value plus VAT, including freight and packing charged on the order
Lithium-cell part | An item with the lithium-cell flag (cell_safety = 1) in the item master
Rate contract | An agreed price for a supplier and item for a period, held in Ledgerline
Direct order (DIR) | An order without a purchase request, allowed only under §3.3
Term | Meaning
Released (RL) | The only status in which the supplier has the order
Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy

4.0 | 2025-04-01 | D. Okafor | Direct-order limit £50,000; UN 38.3 rule for battery packs and hub motors; price tolerance 5%
4.1 | 2026-04-01 | D. Okafor | §6.2 extended to chargers; §6.4 added; §7.2 price tolerance reduced from 5% to 2%

Common errors
Splitting orders across multiple lines or dates to bypass the approval matrix.
Attempting to authorise requisitions while logged in under another member of staff.
Placing commitments verbally with vendors before system sign-off is complete.
Assuming departmental managers can override system settings without IT intervention.
Practical tips
Check user permissions before raising substantial orders to avoid unnecessary workflow holds.
Allow adequate time for senior sign-off when ordering high-value assemblies or plant spares.
Direct any requests for temporary cover or limit amendments to IT well before periods of leave.
6. Supplier qualification
6.2 Battery packs may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate. Hub motors and chargers are not covered by this clause.
6. Supplier qualification

passages.cite: POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.4, § At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that
passages.text:
At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?
Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by
Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you
inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while
an order is pending or in Draft status.
Appendix C. Related documents
• POL-SUP-003 Supplier Policy
• POL-APR-002 Approval Matrix for Purchasing
• AMD-PUR-2026-03 Amendment 3 (direct-order limit from 1 December 2026)
• AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy (certificate window)
• SOP-PUR-001 Supplier onboarding
• SOP-PUR-002 Purchase request to purchase order
• MAN-PUR-72 Ledgerline 7.2 User Manual, Purchasing

messages.content:
You are Ask Northbridge, the assistant on the home page of Northbridge Cycles, Manchester, a maker of e-bikes.
You are talking to Emma Clarke, purchase executive. Today is Monday 26 October 2026.
You can search all of Northbridge's documentation with search_docs: policies, SOPs, amendments, release notes, the
Ledgerline manual and error codes, service definitions, master data exports and e-mails. For any question about a rule,
a procedure, a code or a document, call it first and answer only from the passages it returns, citing each fact as its
cite, for example (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.6, § 6.2). Never state a rule from memory.
- Give the rule in force today. A passage marked superseded or not yet in force does not apply today; if an amendment
  or release note changed an older document, give the current position and say what changed.
- Before you answer, think which of Northbridge's rules the question could depend on (the kind of part, the supplier,
  the amount, the price, the system setting) and search for each of them separately, by its own words: for example
  the supplier by name, then the rule for that kind of part. Battery packs, hub motors and chargers contain or charge
  lithium cells, so the lithium-cell supplier rule applies to them.
- If a passage is "withheld", the answer is in a confidential HR document this user may not see: say so politely and
  that HR (NBC-HR-CONF) can help. Never guess its content.
- If the documents do not answer it, say "That is not in Northbridge's documents" and what is missing.
You cannot see or change Ledgerline ERP yet: no live stock, orders, prices or approvals. If asked for one, say so plainly.
Short, plain replies: two to eight lines, plain text (no bold, no headings). No emoji.

turns.question: What does ERR-PO-0412 mean and how do I fix it?
turns.reply:
ERR-PO-0412 ("TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY") occurs when the tax code entered on a purchase order line does not match the supplier's country recorded in Ledgerline (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1; MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3, p.10, § 17.2). This commonly happens because the Fetch function automatically defaults the tax code to domestic VAT20-UK, even when the supplier is based overseas (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).

To fix it:
1. Check the country code shown in brackets at the end of the error message (e.g. NL) (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
2. For an overseas supplier, change the tax code to reverse charge: VAT20-RC (or VAT5-RC for reduced-rate items) (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
3. If the supplier is registered in the UK, use VAT20-UK (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
4. With your cursor remaining in the line details area, press F8 again to save and recommit the record (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).

passages.cite: QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1, § Recommitting the record
passages.text:
Recommitting the record
• Once the tax code field has been amended, save the entry by pressing F8 again.
• Ensure the cursor remains in the line details area while pressing the key so the validation routine runs against the
amended field.
• If the system accepts the change, the status line will clear and the purchase order will proceed to the next stage.
Avoiding repeated errors
• Frequent occurrences of this message usually indicate that an overseas supplier has been set up with domestic
defaults on their master record.
• If you regularly raise orders for the same overseas vendor and the error persists on fresh orders, notify the purchase
ledger team so the underlying supplier profile can be reviewed.
• Never force an order through using domestic tax codes for an overseas account, as this distorts the tax returns.

passages.cite: QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1, § Reading the country indicator
passages.text:
Reading the country indicator
• Look at the letters shown in brackets at the end of the error message.
• These letters show the country recorded on the supplier account in the system, such as NL for the Netherlands.
• Do not guess the tax treatment from memory; always confirm the location shown in the brackets before altering the
order line.
Selecting the correct tax code
• If the country indicator shows that the supplier is outside the UK, use the reverse charge tax code.
• Apply VAT20-RC for standard goods and materials, or VAT5-RC where the items qualify for the reduced rate.
• If the supplier is registered in the UK, select VAT20-UK instead.
• Check each line item on the purchase order individually, as split deliveries or mixed supplies must carry matching
codes throughout.

Overview of Changes
This patch addresses minor functional and reporting matters within the core purchasing module,
specifically refining message wording and expanding query outputs:
• Messages: The system error text for ERR-PO-0412 has been revised. The previous wording of TAX
REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE is replaced with TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH
SUPPLIER COUNTRY, displaying the supplier country code in brackets at the end of the line. The
underlying tax validation rule and the conditions that trigger the message remain completely
unchanged.
• Purchasing: The purchase order enquiry procedure po_search now returns created_by in its
standard output dataset. This ensures enquiry screens and downstream reporting extracts can
identify the originator directly from search results without requiring secondary lookups against order
headers.

passages.cite: MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3, p.10, § 17. Messages and error codes
passages.text:
17. Messages and error codes
17.1 How to read a message
Every message has a code and a short text, for example ERR-PO-0412 TAX CODE DOES NOT
MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (NL). The code tells you which rule failed; the text in brackets gives
the value that failed it. Errors stop the Save. Warnings do not.
17.2 ERR-PO-0412 Tax code does not match supplier country
Cause: the tax code is for the wrong country. A UK supplier needs a -UK code; a supplier in any other
country needs a reverse-charge -RC code. Fetch always fills VAT20-UK. Remedy: change the tax
code to the -RC code with the same rate (for example VAT20-RC) and save again.

passages.cite: MAN-PUR-70 v7.0, p.3, § 17.2 ERR-PO-0412 TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE
passages.text:
17.2 ERR-PO-0412 TAX REGION DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER STATE
The tax code's region is not the supplier's state. Change the tax code.
Purpose of the Message
This validation prevents purchase orders from being raised with tax treatment that conflicts with the
recorded geographic location of the vendor. When Ledgerline was originally configured, the underlying
accounting structure adopted North American conventions that link tax rates to territorial divisions.
Within the system, every supplier account holds a designated regional assignment alongside its
address records. The message is triggered during purchase order entry whenever the tax code applied
to an individual line or the order header points to a regional authority that disagrees with the master
record for that supplier.
